title: Can You Go to the Shop?
paragraphs: Mum: Hi Sami! I'm at work. Can you go to the shop for me? We need some things for dinner.
Sami: OK, Mum. What do we need?
Mum: We need a litre of milk, six eggs and a kilo of tomatoes. There is a lot of rice at home, so don't buy rice.
Sami: Is there any bread? Mum: No, there isn't. Buy some bread, please. And one packet of pasta.
Sami: Got it! Can I buy a chocolate bar? Mum: Yes, you can. But only one! The money is on the kitchen table. See you at six. Love you!

title: School Science Fair
paragraphs: SCIENCE FAIR! Our school science fair is on Thursday, 12 October, in the main hall. Doors open at 9:00 and close at 1:00.
Students from Grades 4 to 6 show their projects. There are plants, small robots and even a volcano! You can watch, ask questions and take photos.
Parents and families are welcome. Entry is free. You can buy juice and sandwiches at the small stand near the door.
The three best projects win a prize. The judges are our science teachers and a scientist from the university. Please don't touch the projects. Be quiet during the speeches.

title: The Little Blue Bird
paragraphs: A little blue bird lives in a tall tree in a big park. Her name is Luz. Every morning she sings a happy song.
One day, Luz can't sing. She is sad. Her friend, a brown squirrel, comes to the tree. 'What's the matter?' he asks.
'I'm cold and I'm hungry,' says Luz. 'It's raining and I can't find food.' The squirrel gives Luz some nuts. He also brings a big leaf for her head.
Luz eats the nuts. She feels warm and happy. She sings again, and her song is beautiful. 'Thank you, my friend,' she says. 'Friends are great!'

title: My Grandfather, the Fisherman
paragraphs: My grandfather, Don Ernesto, is a fisherman. He is seventy years old and he lives in a small village on the Pacific coast of Ecuador.
Every day, he gets up at four o'clock. He takes his old blue boat and goes to the sea with his friend Beto. They catch fish and sometimes shrimp.
He comes back at noon. My grandmother sells the fish at the market. We eat fish for lunch two or three times a week. It is delicious!
My grandfather isn't rich, but he is very happy. He can tell great stories about the sea. On Sundays, he doesn't work. He plays cards with his friends and drinks coffee.

title: Bus Timetable: Quito to Otavalo
paragraphs: Bus timetable: Quito to Otavalo. Buses leave from Terminal Carcelén. The trip takes about two hours.
Monday to Friday: 6:00, 8:30, 12:00, 3:00 and 6:30 in the evening. The 8:30 bus is very full, so buy your ticket early.
Saturday and Sunday: 7:00, 10:00, 1:00 and 4:00. On Saturday there is also a bus at 5:30. Otavalo's famous market is on Saturday.
Tickets cost $3.50. Children under six travel free. There is a toilet on the bus, but there isn't Wi-Fi. Please arrive 15 minutes before the bus leaves.

title: A Rainy Sunday
paragraphs: Sunday, 9 June. It is raining today, so I'm at home all day. I'm bored, but I have a plan!
In the morning, I'm cleaning my room with my brother, Leo. There are clothes on the floor and books under the bed. Now my room is tidy.
It's two o'clock. Leo is playing a video game and Mum is cooking soup in the kitchen. The smell is great! I'm drawing a picture of our dog, Max. He is sleeping on the sofa.
Later, we watch a film together. It is our Sunday tradition. I like rainy Sundays after all!

title: Hello from Buenos Aires
paragraphs: Hi Dani! I'm in Buenos Aires with my cousins. It's a huge city, and it's very busy. There are cars, buses and people everywhere!
Today we are walking in La Boca. The houses are red, yellow and blue. There are artists in the street. Some of them paint and some play music.
The food here is great. I love the pizza and the ice cream. My cousin Julián loves ice cream, too. He eats two every day!
The weather is warm and windy. I'm wearing shorts and a T-shirt. I can't send you a photo, so I'm sending this card. See you soon! Pablo

title: Polar Ice Cream
paragraphs: Welcome to Polar Ice Cream! We have fourteen flavours. Come in and try our fruit and chocolate ice creams.
Flavours: strawberry, vanilla, chocolate, mango, lemon and coconut. Every Monday there is a new flavour. This Monday it is passion fruit!
Prices: one scoop $1.50, two scoops $2.50, three scoops $3.50. Cone or cup? You choose. A cone with chocolate on top costs 50 cents more.
Milkshakes are $3. We are open every day from 11:00 to 9:00. On Sundays, children under ten get a free scoop with an adult.

title: Welcome to My Room
focus: There is / there are; prepositions of place
paragraphs: Welcome to my room! It's small, but I love it. My room is on the second floor of our house, and it has a big window.
There is a bed next to the window. Above the bed, there are two shelves with my books and a small plant. There is a desk in front of the bed, and there is a lamp on the desk.
There is a poster of my favourite singer on the wall. There isn't a TV, but there is a guitar in the corner. I play it every evening.
My cat, Nube, sleeps on the chair. The room isn't tidy now, because there are socks on the floor! What's in your room? Write to me!

title: Hello from Canada
paragraphs: Hello Sofía,
My name is Ryan and I'm twelve years old. I'm from Vancouver, in Canada. I'm your new pen pal!
I live with my mum, my dad and my sister, Emily. She is eight. We have a dog called Bella and two fish. Do you have any pets?
At school, I like Science and Music. I play the drums in the school band. In my free time, I play ice hockey and I ride my bike. It's cold in Canada in winter, but I love the snow.
Is it hot in your city? What do you do after school? Please write soon and send me a photo!
Best wishes,
Ryan
